description: "Rivet diagnostic RV2014 (warning): `.bind(…)` inside an object literal a resumable closure reaches (resume). What triggers it and how to fix it."

**Severity:** warning · **Area:** Resume (`RV2xxx`) · **Quick fix:** none

## Message

The diagnostic reads:

```text
`.bind(…)` inside an object literal may not resume (a native bound function is not serializable): keep the bound function in a local constant (`const g = f.bind(…)`) and store `g`; an object with its own `bind` is fine
```

## How to fix

Bind into a local constant first and store it by name: `const inc = add.bind(null, 1); const api = { inc };`.

## Example

```tsx avoid nocheck
import { signal } from "@rivetjs/reactivity";
export function A() {
  const n = signal(0);
  const add = (by: number) => n.set(n() + by);
  const api = { inc: add.bind(null, 1) };
  return <b onClick={() => api.inc()}>{n()}</b>;
}
```

```tsx prefer
import { signal } from "@rivetjs/reactivity";
export function A() {
  const n = signal(0);
  const add = (by: number) => n.set(n() + by);
  const inc = add.bind(null, 1);
  const api = { inc };
  return <b onClick={() => api.inc()}>{n()}</b>;
}
```

## When it is reported

Resume mode (Function Bridge T10). A warning, only when a resumable closure reaches the property: it captures the whole object or reads that key (`api.inc()`); a handler reading another key (`api.k`) is clean.
